summary: Pursued the last registered necessary gap: reachability of the snapshot-boundary precondition through a legal multi-node history rather than a seeded RPC. Registered investigation @q-reachability-history and experiment update-05.json (harness assurance_generated_test.go, now a five-node real-history harness): MakeClusterCustom with a Restore-counting FSM, isolate the leader from the three non-partner peers, have it replicate an uncommitted suffix to exactly the partner, wait for a successor among the other three, apply one command so the successor has something to snapshot, snapshot there, heal, then sample the partner's Restore count and applied index at 300 ms and 1500 ms. Local construction feedback gave a genuine negative result, recorded rather than suppressed: divergent_prefix {base_index 2, leader_last_index 6, partner_last_index 6, partner_replicated_uncommitted true} and new_leader_snapshot {divergence_index 3, snapshot_index 4, new_leader_term 3, old_leader_term 2} show the follower did hold term-2 entries at indices 3..6 while the term-3 successor snapshotted inside that window, yet the heal converged with restores_before/early/late all 0 and the follower's applied and last index at 4, i.e. ordinary AppendEntries repaired the suffix and InstallSnapshot was never needed. The interpretation is recorded as unresolved with the contrary observation, a candidate explanation (the mismatch-driven nextIndex rewinds may have reached a prev-log index the successor still retained, so truncation happened before SEND_SNAP) and the limitation that this is a different configuration from the retained witness CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7, which therefore remains asserted on its own basis. Structural validation returned valid=true.
